cards.title: Common Grammatical Mistakes
rule: Common Grammatical Mistakes & L1 Interference Traps

Definition: L1 Interference and Grammatical Errors (ናይ ቀዳማይ ቋንቋ ጽልዋን ስሩዓት ሰዋስዋዊ ጌጋታትን) refers to the systematic syntactic, morphological, and orthographic errors made by Tigrinya-native speakers due to the negative transfer of Semitic linguistic structures and phonology into English.

Negative language transfer (ኣሉታዊ ምስግጋር ቋንቋ) occurs when the grammar, phonology, or word order of a student's native language conflicts with the rules of the target language. Since Tigrinya is a highly inflected Subject-Object-Verb ($$\text{S-O-V}$$) Semitic language, and English is an analytical Subject-Verb-Object ($$\text{S-V-O}$$) Germanic language, Tigrinya speakers face systematic, predictable interference traps. Rather than treating these errors as random, uncoordinated mistakes, this chapter provides a systematic diagnostic framework to identify, analyze, and neutralize these traps, helping students secure maximum marks on national matriculation examinations.

cards.title: Notes
body: Common Grammatical Mistakes & L1 Interference Traps

Definition: L1 Interference and Grammatical Errors (ናይ ቀዳማይ ቋንቋ ጽልዋን ስሩዓት ሰዋስዋዊ ጌጋታትን) refers to the systematic syntactic, morphological, and orthographic errors made by Tigrinya-native speakers due to the negative transfer of Semitic linguistic structures and phonology into English.

Negative language transfer (ኣሉታዊ ምስግጋር ቋንቋ) occurs when the grammar, phonology, or word order of a student's native language conflicts with the rules of the target language. Since Tigrinya is a highly inflected Subject-Object-Verb ($$\text{S-O-V}$$) Semitic language, and English is an analytical Subject-Verb-Object ($$\text{S-V-O}$$) Germanic language, Tigrinya speakers face systematic, predictable interference traps. Rather than treating these errors as random, uncoordinated mistakes, this chapter provides a systematic diagnostic framework to identify, analyze, and neutralize these traps, helping students secure maximum marks on national matriculation examinations.

A prominent syntax error is the Redundant Double Subject ($$\times \text{Subject Noun} + \text{Subject Pronoun} + \text{Verb}$$). In Tigrinya, verbs are conjugated with obligatorily embedded pronominal subject markers (e.g., "ኣቦይ ሓረስታይ [ንሱ] እዩ"). This structure makes native speakers feel that stating the noun subject ("My father") requires immediate pronoun reinforcement ("he") before the verb, resulting in ungrammatical sentences like "My father *he* is a hardworking farmer." In standard English, a clause must strictly contain only a single subject referent per verb; therefore, writing "My father is a hardworking farmer" is the only correct form.

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct and free from L1 double-subject errors?

steps.text: In English, a clause must contain only a single subject referent per verb.
The noun phrase 'My elder brother' is the subject of 'is studying'.

cards.answer: My elder brother is studying civil engineering at university.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct and free from L1 double-subject errors?

options.A: My elder brother he is studying civil engineering at university.
options.B: My elder brother is studying civil engineering at university.
options.C: My elder brother, he is studying civil engineering at university.
options.D: My elder brother him is studying civil engineering at university.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
In English, a clause must contain only a single subject referent per verb. The noun phrase 'My elder brother' is the subject of 'is studying'.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Options A and C contain a redundant pronoun 'he' immediately following the noun subject. This is a classic double-subject error caused by Tigrinya verb conjugation habits. Option B correctly eliminates the redundant pronoun.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ኣብ እንግሊዘኛ ወግዒ ሓደ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ሓደ ዋና ባእታ (Subject) ጥራይ እዩ ዝወስድ። 'My elder brother' (ሓወይ) ባዕሉ እኹል ዋና ባእታ ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ድሕሪኡ 'he' (ንሱ) ምጥቃም ድርብ ዋና ባእታ (Double Subject) ዝበሃል ዓቢ ጌጋ ይፈጥር። ስለዚ ቅኑዕ መልሲ Option B እዩ።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: Because the physics laboratory was locked yesterday afternoon, ________ we were unable to perform the experiment.

steps.text: 'Because' is a subordinating conjunction at the beginning of the sentence to connect the clauses.
In English, only one conjunction can connect two clauses; adding a second is a double-conjunction error.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Because the physics laboratory was locked yesterday afternoon, ________ we were unable to perform the experiment.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Because' is a subordinating conjunction at the beginning of the sentence to connect the clauses. In English, only one conjunction can connect two clauses; adding a second is a double-conjunction error.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often choose 'so' (Option A) because in Tigrinya, it is natural to pair cause with result (e.g., 'ስለ ዝሓመመ፡ ስለዚ...'). Option D is correct because no extra connector is allowed.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ኣብ መጀመርታ እቲ ምሉእ ሓሳብ 'Because' (ምኽንያቱ/ስለ ዝ-) ዝብል መተሓሓዚ ስለ ዘሎ፡ ኣብቲ ካልኣይ ሓረግ 'so' (ስለዚ) ምጥቃም ዓቢ ናይ ድርብ መስተጻምር ጌጋ (double-conjunction error) ይፈጥር። ስለዚ ቅኑዕ መልሲ Option D ([No connector] - ዋላ ሓደ ቃል ኣየድልይን) እዩ።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: Identify the sentence that contains a copula verb omission error caused by L1 interference:

steps.text: Every English sentence expressing a state of being requires an explicit copula verb ('is', 'are', 'was', 'were') between the subject and the adjective complement.
In Option C, the copula verb 'is' is completely missing.

cards.answer: My brother very hardworking and always studies late.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Identify the sentence that contains a copula verb omission error caused by L1 interference:

options.A: She is an exceptionally clever student in our class.
options.B: They are from the southern region of Eritrea.
options.C: My brother very hardworking and always studies late.
options.D: We were delighted to receive your invitation.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
Every English sentence expressing a state of being requires an explicit copula verb ('is', 'are', 'was', 'were') between the subject and the adjective complement.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
In Option C, the copula verb 'is' is completely missing. In Tigrinya, the copula can sometimes be omitted in speech, leading students to translate directly as 'My brother very hardworking...', which is incorrect. Option C is the target error.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ኣብ እንግሊዘኛ 'ምዃን' ዘመልክቱ ሓገዝቲ ግሶች (copula verbs - is, are) ወግዒ ክጸሓፉ ኣለዎም። ኣብ Option C 'My brother [is] very hardworking' ክኸውን ስለ ዝነበሮ፡ እቲ ግሲ ብምጥፋኡ ጌጋ ኣለዎ። ተማሃሮ ብስሕተት 'My brother very...' ኢሎም ክጽሕፉ ይረኣዩ እዮም።

questions.q: Identify the sentence that contains a copula verb omission error caused by L1 interference:
questions.label: 3. Identify the sentence that contains a copula verb omission e

options.A: She is an exceptionally clever student in our class.
options.B: They are from the southern region of Eritrea.
options.C: My brother very hardworking and always studies late.
options.D: We were delighted to receive your invitation.

why: Answer C: My brother very hardworking and always studies late.
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
Every English sentence expressing a state of being requires an explicit copula verb ('is', 'are', 'was', 'were') between the subject and the adjective complement.
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The program coordinator congratulated the candidates ________ achieving top scores on the ESSLCE.
questions.label: 4. The program coordinator congratulated the candidates _______
why: Answer B: on
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The verb 'congratulate' strictly requires the preposition 'on' followed by a noun or gerund: $$\text{congratulate} + \text{someone} + \text{on} + \text{something}$$.
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The administrative assistant provided us with many useful ________ regarding the registration process.
questions.label: 5. The administrative assistant provided us with many useful __
why: Answer B: pieces of advice
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Advice' is strictly uncountable and cannot be pluralized with an '-s' suffix. To express plurality, we must use partitive phrases like 'pieces of advice'.
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: Identify the sentence that displays correct pronoun placement for a separable phrasal verb:
questions.label: 6. Identify the sentence that displays correct pronoun placemen

options.A: Please turn off the light before you leave.
options.B: Please turn the light off before you leave.
options.C: Please turn it off before you leave.
options.D: Please turn off it before you leave.

why: Answer D: Please turn off it before you leave.
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**

'Turn off' is a transitive separable phrasal verb. Noun objects can go in the middle or at the end. Pronoun objects ('it') **must** go in the middle: $$\text{Verb} + \text{Pronoun} + \text{Particle}$$.
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The chemistry instructor told the students ________ any of the chemical solutions.
questions.label: 7. The chemistry instructor told the students ________ any of t
why: Answer B: not to touch
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
This is a reported negative command. Negative commands are reported using the structure: $$\text{reporting verb} + \text{object} + \text{not to} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$.
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: Choose the sentence that displays correct English word order ($$\text{S-V-O}$$):
questions.label: 8. Choose the sentence that displays correct English word order

options.A: The doctor the patient examined yesterday afternoon.
options.B: The doctor examined the patient yesterday afternoon.
options.C: Yesterday afternoon the doctor the patient examined.
options.D: Examined the doctor the patient yesterday afternoon.

why: Answer B: The doctor examined the patient yesterday afternoon.
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
English requires a strict Subject-Verb-Object ($$\text{S-V-O}$$) pattern. The subject is 'The doctor', the verb is 'examined', and the direct object is 'the patient'.
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: When I was a young boy living in the village, I was extremely afraid ________ wild dogs.
questions.label: 9. When I was a young boy living in the village, I was extremel
why: Answer C: of
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The adjective 'afraid' must strictly be paired with the preposition 'of' ($$\text{afraid} + \text{of} + \text{noun}$$).
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: Identify the option that displays correct spelling for the modified word class:
questions.label: 10. Identify the option that displays correct spelling for the m

options.A: We had a delicious lunch in the school dinning room.
options.B: We had a delicious lunch in the school dining room.
options.C: We had a delicious lunch in the school daining room.
options.D: We had a delicious lunch in the school dineing room.

why: Answer B: We had a delicious lunch in the school dining room.
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The verb 'dine' ends in a single silent 'e'. When adding the suffix '-ing', the 'e' is dropped to form 'dining' (/ˈdaɪnɪŋ/).
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**

options.B: I don't knows anything about it.

similar.a: I have known him since childhood.

similar.q: Complete: He has worked here ____ five years.

options.A: She has been living here since 2015.
options.B: She has been living here for 2015.

why: Answer A: She has been living here since 2015.
"since 2015" (a starting point) requires a perfect tense.
Use the present perfect (continuous): has been living.
"for" is used with periods (for ten years), not points in time.

questions.label: 14. Which sentence is correct?

similar.q: Correct: Because he was late, so he ran.
similar.a: Because he was late, he ran.

similar.q: Correct: Despite he was tired, he worked.
similar.a: Although he was tired, he worked.

options.A: Although it was raining, but we went out.
options.B: Although raining, but we went out.
options.C: Despite it was raining, we went out.
options.D: Although it was raining, we went out.

why: Answer D: Although it was raining, we went out.
Use only one connector per link: "Although ... but" is a double conjunction.
"Despite" cannot be followed by a full clause.
The first option is correct.

questions.q: Correct the error: "He explained me the problem."
questions.label: 15. Correct the error: "He explained me the problem."

similar.a: She described the house to me.

similar.q: Correct: Please suggest me a book.
similar.a: Please suggest a book to me.

questions.answer: He explained the problem to me.
why: "explain" cannot take a person directly as an indirect object.
The pattern is "explain something to someone".
So: He explained the problem to me.

why: Answer A: my family and I; We swam
"my family and ___" is the subject, so use "I".

Only the first option fixes both errors.
